lines.trans: All the paintings were painted by me personally.
Any of them can be purchased.
The money will go to charity.
And this right here is my pride.
It is called 'Ex-Husband.'
And I will bring champagne.
I see he still has not confessed to you.
Lena, I do not want to deceive you.
My first husband is Victor Petrovich.
Which Victor Petrovich?
Because he is a coward and a liar.
They called me from work, I will go.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'paintings' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: All the paintings were painted by me personally.

examples.text: На кухне картины Дали и Ван Гога.
examples.trans: Paintings by Dalí and Van Gogh in the kitchen.
Beautiful paintings hang in the museum.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'painted / written', paired with 'писать'.

examples.trans: All the paintings were painted by me personally.
He wrote a statement.
Write to me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: All the paintings were painted by me personally.
Great, so you know everything.

examples.text: Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: Anikeev came here in person, and what?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'any', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We are exchanging curious facts, after all.
Any of them can be purchased.

examples.text: Когда теряешь любовь, жизнь лишается всякого смысла.
examples.trans: When you lose love, life loses all meaning.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: That simply cannot be!
Maybe she was joking?

examples.text: А может, это ребёнок не от меня, правда?
examples.trans: Maybe this child really is not mine?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'обрести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to purchase / acquire'.

examples.trans: Any of them can be purchased.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и приобрести вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to purchase on time.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'money' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The money will go to charity.

examples.text: В тот день, когда ты отказалась выходить за меня замуж.
examples.trans: On that day when you refused to marry me.
Bad day?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: The money will go to charity.

examples.text: Мне с работы позвонили, я пойду.
examples.trans: They called me from work, I will go.
Very sad, I will go then.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We need to talk!
I know that you are pregnant!
You have such a wonderful boss.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'charity' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The money will go to charity.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть благотворительность.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always charity.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Vika, wait!
We need to talk!
I know that you are pregnant!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Poor girl, what a misfortune.

examples.text: А я вот себе туфли новые купил.
examples.trans: And I just bought myself new shoes.

examples.text: Много свободного времени, вот и занимается ерундой.
examples.trans: Lots of free time, so she busies herself with nonsense.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

examples.text: Я готов быть отцом этого ребёнка.
examples.trans: I am ready to be the father of this child.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Но я точно знаю, что ребёнок мой.
examples.trans: But I know for sure that the child is mine.

examples.text: Дело в том, что это мой ребёнок.
examples.trans: The thing is that this is my child.
My first husband is Victor Petrovich.

meanings.note: Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common feminine noun meaning 'pride' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And this right here is my pride.
He is the pride of our family.

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'зываться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is called'.

examples.trans: What's this town called?
The operation is called Golden Yard.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('former, ex-').

examples.trans: You blabber about your ex-husband.

examples.text: Моя бывшая беременна, говорит, что не от меня.
examples.trans: My ex is pregnant and says it is not mine.
It is called 'Ex-Husband.'

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'husband' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You blabber about your ex-husband.

examples.text: От тебя же все мужики сбегают.
examples.trans: All men run away from you.
It is called 'Ex-Husband.'

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will bring', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: And I will bring champagne.
What did you bring into the flat?
He brought you a dog.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'champagne' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: And I will bring champagne.
Open the champagne!
A glass of champagne, please.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.text: Я её после этого не видел.
examples.trans: I did not see her after that.
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Eleonora had an unhappy marriage.
She is a good one you have.

examples.text: Слушай, Эля, ты думаешь, я ничего не понимаю?
examples.trans: Listen, Elya, do you think I understand nothing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You have such a wonderful boss.

examples.text: Так сбежал, что ты до него не доберёшься.
examples.trans: He ran so far that you will not reach him.

examples.text: У чувака на форуме такая же проблема.
examples.trans: A guy on the forum has the exact same problem.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!
Vika, wait!
We need to talk!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Do not drink anything for a minute!

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.
This is not your child.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'знаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'confessed / admitted', paired with 'признаваться'.

examples.text: Он хотел в чём-то мне признаться.
examples.trans: He wanted to confess something to me.
Well, did he confess?
He confessed to everything.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!

examples.text: Почему ты ничего мне не рассказывал?
examples.trans: Why did you not tell me anything?
In a divorce, two people are always at fault.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Он хотел в чём-то мне признаться.
examples.trans: He wanted to confess something to me.
Kostya wanted to cover for me.
I want coffee.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'манывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to deceive', paired with 'обмануть'.

examples.text: Лена, я не хочу тебя обманывать.
examples.trans: Lena, I do not want to deceive you.
Everybody cheats her.
Don't lie to me!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.trans: My first husband is Victor Petrovich.
No, I am seeing her for the first time.
This is my first day.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('what').

examples.trans: How noble.
As a subordinate.

examples.text: Это какую правду Кате не расскажешь?
examples.trans: What truth can you not tell Katya?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'тому').

examples.text: Потому что он трус и лжец.
examples.trans: Because he is a coward and a liar.
And why did you not confess afterward?

examples.text: Потому что я повар. Я настоящий профессионал.
examples.trans: Because I am a cook. I am a true professional.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what, that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I know that you are pregnant!
The main thing is that I am here.

examples.text: Тем более, что ты уже начал.
examples.trans: Especially since you have already started.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'coward' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Потому что он трус и лжец.
examples.trans: Because he is a coward and a liar.
We will cope with all the difficulties.
Because you're a coward!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'liar' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Потому что он трус и лжец.
examples.trans: Because he is a coward and a liar.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть лжец.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always liar.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with / from', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The rookie has returned!
Who told you?

examples.text: Не важно, кто мне это сказал.
examples.trans: It does not matter who told me this.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'job, work' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Work does not wait, it is time to run.

examples.text: Мне с работы позвонили, я пойду.
examples.trans: They called me from work, I will go.
I'm going to work.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning '(they) called', paired with 'звонить'.

examples.text: Мне с работы позвонили, я пойду.
examples.trans: They called me from work, I will go.
Call me this evening.
I'll call tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'слаждаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'enjoy'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и наслаждаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and enjoy on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют наслаждаться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to enjoy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'кусство'). Common neuter noun meaning 'art' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я знаю, как ты относишься к современному искусству.
examples.trans: I know how you feel about modern art.
You enjoy the art.
Read The Art of War, by Sun Tzu!
